_about: The podcast tracker (podcast-tracker.html, assets/podcasts.js). See CLAUDE.md, "Podcast Tracker". A row is one episode: n (null for an unnumbered extra), title, kind (bonus/extract/special), date (release, New York), catalogueDate (the * dates), href, note, done.

podcasts.name: The Rest Is History
podcasts.subtitle: Classical history & mythology
podcasts.lede: A chronological listening guide with subscriber extras.
guide: Read from section 01 onward. Section 01 is a mythological prologue; 02 supplies optional ancient-world background; 03-06 form the historical sequence. Section 07 covers society and later interpretations. Further subscriber discussions follow by subject.
BONUS identifies unnumbered subscriber extras or livestreams. EXTRACT identifies book readings.

Each part has its own number and release date. Series remain adjacent in historical order. Unnumbered bonuses have no official main-series episode number; their exact titles and dates are the identifiers.

notes.title: Scope
text: It covers dedicated classical episodes plus substantial, identifiable ancient-world segments in mixed extras. The focus is Greece, Rome, Persia, Carthage, their mythological and literary worlds, and late antiquity. Earlier Egypt, Mesopotamia and prehistory are included as context; Arthur and China are explicitly optional. This is not an exhaustive index of every fleeting classical reference in every general Q&A.

Every title links to its official episode/series listing or, for a few older feed items, its podcast page. Sign in with your membership when prompted. An access prompt on a website does not by itself establish that a numbered episode is absent from the public feed.

notes.title: Release-date method
text: Release dates: numbered episodes use original public-feed timestamps converted to America/New_York when available. An asterisk (*) identifies a date displayed by the official catalogue or publisher listing where no feed timestamp was established; this includes members-only items and early access. Your subscriber feed may show an earlier date than the public release.

The date beside an episode is its release date, not the historical date of its subject. Main-feed publication timestamps are converted to America/New_York; this can fall on the previous calendar day relative to Britain or UTC. The original feed is used instead of migrated website dates such as 27 November 2021 that were applied to many older episodes.

Dates marked * are the calendar date shown by the official episode catalogue or publisher listing. They may represent a members' release, livestream listing or later edition. A timestamp was not established for those dates. Member early access and public release are therefore not assumed to be identical. The January 1 Nero special was published at 02:00 UTC on 1 January 2022, which is 31 December 2021 in New York.

notes.title: Numbering and identification
text: Hadrian and Antinous is episode 340 despite an inconsistent number on its webpage. Greek Myths is 602-605; the series page duplicates 603 for Part 3. Use the part order. The January 1 Nero/Byzantium special is unnumbered; episode 151 is Valentine's Day. The two Pompeii episodes, 16 and 355, are distinct.

King Arthur is listed as 713-716 on the official series page, including the fourth part in the current members catalogue. Publication and series-header dates on some migrated pages are inconsistent; this guide uses verified episode numbers and series order instead of relying on those headers.
